# cpanel_log_settings (Resource)

Manages the cPanel account's raw access log archival settings. Removing the resource restores the complete settings observed when Terraform first took ownership.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cpanel_log_settings" "account" {
  archive_logs   = true
  prune_archives = true
  retention_days = -1
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `archive_logs` (Boolean) Whether cPanel archives processed access logs in the account home directory.
- `prune_archives` (Boolean) Whether cPanel removes the previous month's archived logs.
- `retention_days` (Number) The configured retention period. `-1` uses the server default, `0` retains logs indefinitely, and positive values are days.

### Read-Only

- `account` (String) The singleton account identity, always `account`.
- `effective_retention_days` (Number) The effective number of retention days reported by cPanel. `0` means indefinitely.
- `restore_archive_logs` (Boolean) Whether log archival was enabled before Terraform management.
- `restore_prune_archives` (Boolean) Whether archive pruning was enabled before Terraform management.
- `restore_retention_days` (Number) The retention configuration that Terraform restores when the resource is removed. `-1` means the server default.
- `using_default_retention` (Boolean) Whether the account uses the server-wide retention period.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import cpanel_log_settings.account account
```
